title: FEI Tribunal Settlement Agreement Case C25-0034 Case 2025BS08 QUETZALCOATL Z - Ms Saree GORDON SOLANKI
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY THE FEI TRIBUNAL
20 March 2026
In the matter of
FÉDÉRATION EQUESTRE INTERNATIONALE (the “FEI”)
vs.
Ms. Saree Gordon SOLANKI –Person Responsible (the “PR”)
together the “Parties”
(Reference No. FEI Tribunal: C25-0034 SOLANKI)
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Mr José A. Rodríguez Álvarez (MEX), Sole Panel Member
FEI Case number: 2025/BS08
Horse/ID/NF: QUETZALCOATL Z/107IK47/USA
Person Responsible/ID/NF: SAREE GORDON SOLANKI/10085672/ISR
Event/Date: CS13* Temecula CA (USA) (20/05/2025 - 24/05/2025)
Date of sample collection: 24.05.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): O-desmethylvenlafaxine (a metabolite of Venlafaxine)
Bar Code No.: 1609751
1

All the words used in this Final Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously defined
have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the FEI General Regulations (the “GRs”)
and Statutes, the 2025 Equine Prohibited Substance List (the “Prohibited List”) and the Equine
Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”). The Equine Anti-Doping
Rules (the “EAD Rules”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the “ECM Rules”) are set out
in the EADCMRs.
I. INTRODUCTION
1. This final Decision pertains to the FEI case 2025/BS08 QUETZALCOATL Z. In this matter, the
FEI notified the PR of a violation of Article 2.1 (The presence of a Banned Substance and/or its
Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) of the EAD Rules. This violation was based on the
positive finding of O-desmethylvenlafaxine in the Sample of the Horse QUETZALCOATL Z (the
“Horse”) which was collected at the CSIO4* - CSI3*- Temecula CA (USA) held between 20 and
24 May 2025 (the “Event”).
2. The FEI and the PR reached a settlement agreement on 26 January 2026 (the “Settlement
Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement and its Exhibits are hereby incorporated by
reference into this final Decision.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions:
3. The following regulations are applicable to the present case:
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2025
(“GRs”).
▪ Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective 1
January 2025 (“EADCMRs”). The EADCMRs are divided into the Equine Anti-Doping Rules
(the “EADRs”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the “ECMRs”).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 3rd Edition, 1 February 2025 (“the IRs”).
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21st November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
III. PARTIES
2

4. Ms. Saree Gordon SOLANKI (FEI ID 10085672) is a rider in the discipline of Jumping and PR in
accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs. She competed with the Horse at the Event. The PR
is a member of the Israeli Equestrian Federation (the “ISR-NF”), the latter being a member of
the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the ECM Rules.
5. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving, Endurance and
Vaulting.
6. The FEI and the PR are together referred to as the Parties.
IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
7. The Horse was tested during the Event, and the analysis of the urine and blood samples
revealed the presence of O-desmethylvenlafaxine, an antidepressant used to treat depression
and anxiety, at an estimated concentration of 3.5 ng/mL. O-desmethylvenlafaxine is a
metabolite of Venlafaxine. Venlafaxine is classified as a Banned Substance under the EADRs.
8. By Notification Letter dated 23 June 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the PR of
a potential violation of Article 2.1 of the EADRs (Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its
Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) based on the findings of O-desmethylvenlafaxine in
the sample. The PR was also notified in said letter that he was provisionally suspended under
Article 7.4.1 of the EADRs, and the Horse was also provisionally suspended for two months from
the date of the Notification Letter.
9. In the Notification Letter the PR was also provided the right to request an analysis of the B
Sample within 10 days of the Notification Letter. The PR requested the B Sample analysis
within the deadline as outlined in the Notification Letter. By letter dated 15 July 2025, the FEI
confirmed that the analysis of the B Sample which reconfirmed the Adverse Analytical Finding
(the “AAF”) and maintained the alleged violation as specified in the Notification Letter. By
same letter, the FEI granted the PR fourteen (14) days either to admit the violation or to
provide an explanation to the alleged violation (such deadline was extended until 3 October
2025 due to communications between the FEI and PR as set out in the motivated decision
of 20 January 2026.)
3

10. On 3 October 2025, the PR provided an explanation to the FEI and submitted that the source
of the O-desmethylvenlafaxine in the Sample was an environmental contamination and
admitted the EADR violation.
11. In particular, the PR furthered that during the Event, which was held at Galway Downs
Equestrian Center (“Galway Downs”), the Horse stayed in Stall #28, in Barn #9 (“Stall #28”). She
claimed that, on balance of probabilities, Stall #28 was contaminated with Venlafaxine and that
was the source of the AAF, for the following reasons:
• Shortly after notification of the AAF, on 27 June 2025, the PR contacted the Manager
of Galway Downs, and asked him to lock Stall #28 so that it could be preserved for
future analysis;
• The Manager did so and confirmed that Stall #28 was locked from 27 June 2025
until the PR was able to arrange for samples from Stall #28 to be collected for
analysis, on 6 August 2025;
• Several wipe samples were collected from Stall #28 on 6 August 2025. One of those
samples (“Wipe-7”), which was taken from the floor of Stall #28, tested positive for
Venlafaxine;
• Thus, the Horse’s stall at the Event was contaminated with Venlafaxine;
• The PR, along with other witnesses present, submitted that the stalls at the Event
were unclean, unsanitary and were some of the dirtiest stalls they have ever
encountered at an FEI or USEF competition.
12. On 10 November 2025, the FEI indicated that, having considered the PR’s explanation and
supporting evidence, it consented to the lifting of the PR’s provisional suspension.
13. On 12 November 2025, the PR requested the urgent lifting of the provisional suspension in
accordance with Article 7.4.4(ii) of the EADRs, with the FEI’s consent.
14. On 14 November 2025, the FEI Tribunal lifted the PR’s provisional suspension.
15. On 11 December 2025, the FEI confirmed that it accepted that the PR bore No Fault or
Negligence for the EADR violation.
16. On 26 January 2026, the FEI submitted the Settlement Agreement with Exhibits for the
approval of the FEI Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) and requested for a panel to be appointed for
the purpose or review and approval of the said Settlement Agreement.
4

17. On 4 February 2026, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a sole panel
member (the “Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The Parties were asked to provide
any objections to the constitution of the Panel by 9 February 2026. On 5 February 2026, the
FEI and PR, respectively, provided their confirmation of no objections to the constitution of
the Panel.
V. ACCEPTED TERMS
18. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and is
subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
19. The PR admitted the EADR Rule Violation and accepted the following terms (the “Accepted
Terms”) in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR:
(a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 (Presence of a Banned Substance in a Horse’s
Sample) of the EADR;
(b) The PR has established, on the balance of probabilities, how O-desmethylvenlafaxine
entered the Horse’s system;
(c) The PR has established that she bore No Fault or Negligence for the rule violation in
accordance with Article 10.5 of the EADR;
(d) Therefore, no period of Ineligibility shall be imposed on the PR;
(e) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes, in
accordance with Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR;
(f) The PR shall not incur any fine;
(g) No other sanctions will apply in this case;
(h) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with these
proceedings (and the PR will bear the costs of the B Sample analysis in the amount of CHF
1,000);
(i) Pursuant to Article 10.9.2 of the EADR, this violation of the EADR shall not Case 2025/BS08
QUETZALCOATL Z be considered a prior violation for the purpose of Article 10.9 (Multiple
Violations) of the EADR.
VI. DECISION
20. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
159 of the GRs, the EADRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member of the ISR-NF, which
is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs.
5

21. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement and the
Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel accepts that the FEI found that the PR had established,
on a balance of probabilities, how O-desmethylvenlafaxine entered the Horse’s system.
22. The Hearing Panel further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on the terms
for the closure of the proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, as detailed
under Section V of this Decision.
23. The Hearing Panel confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement comply
with the EADRs and finds no grounds to object to them.
24. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADRs this Final
Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement Agreement are
a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter of these proceedings.
25. The Settlement Agreement and this Decision are not subject to appeal under Article 13 of
the EADRs.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The NF of the PR: Yes
c. Any other: USA-NF
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
____________________________________________________________________
Mr José A. Rodríguez Álvarez, Sole Panel Member
